kurz: Dissolved sugar wants to form crystals again. Even a single grain can set off a chain reaction.
bild_im_kopf: Like dominoes: when one falls, they all fall. A sugar crystal on the side of the pan is enough as the first domino.
was_passiert: Hot syrup holds far more dissolved [[zucker|sugar]] than it can hold when cold. As it cools, or when stirred, the sugar [[molekuel|molecules]] attach to any crystal present, and the syrup turns grainy. Acid, honey or [[glukosesirup|glucose syrup]] disrupt crystal formation and keep caramel smooth.
warum_wichtig: Explains why caramel suddenly turns sandy, and why with fudge you control crystallisation on purpose.
faustregeln: Do not stir while sugar is boiling. Swirl instead of stirring.
Wash crystals off the side of the pan with a wet brush.
A spoonful of glucose syrup or a little lemon juice prevents graininess.
